new_statements.translation: All the languages [the ten studied, including Mosange = Ndolo] attest two basic simple tones, the high tone (H), which we write with the acute accent, and the low tone (L), written with the grave accent. From these two basic tones derive two main contour tones: rising (M) and falling (D). The tone-bearing mora is the vowel in almost all the languages studied. [...] (48) H ... Mosange li-só 'eye' ... (49) L ... Mosange wo 'you' ... (53) H-H ... Mosange li-tálé 'stone' ... (p.44) Phonologically distinctive vowel length, i.e. an opposition between long and short vowels, does not exist in the languages studied.

The Mosange examples follow on pp.62-67 exactly as reported: (48) H mosángé li-só 'oeil', (49) B mosángé wo 'toi', (53) H-H mosángé li…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Ndolo (Mosange variety) is described as a two-tone language (H, L, plus rising/falling contours on vowels) with lexically free tone patterns on noun stems (H, L, HH, HL, LL, LH, LLL, LLH, LHL attested) and no distinctive vowel length; the source makes no statement about word stress or accent, so no stress position can be extracted.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. Tonal notes only: Mosange lacks rising-tone monosyllabic noun stems and lacks H-H-H, H-B-B and H-H-B trisyllabic schemes in Donzo's corpus (pp.63-66).
new_statements.domain_note: Statements concern lexical tone on nominal stems (prefixes excluded) in citation forms; comparative overview chapter covering ten languages, Mosange data from the author's own fieldwork. No word- or phrase-level stress discussed anywhere in the 466-page thesis (a full-text search for stress/accent full text: 'accent' occurs only as the name of tone diacritics).
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted source describes 'mosángé', the lect of the Mosange groupement on the Saw river (secteur Ndolo-Liboko, territoire de Budjala); Glottolog lists Mosange as an alternative name of Ndolo [ndl] (ndol1238) and links Donzo 2015 to ndl via 'Mosángé = Ndolo [ndl]'. The other described Ndolo variety is Bokala ('Bokala-Ndolo C36g', Bonzoi 1999; Bonzoi & Motingea 2013), not seen. Note that Zelenge 2000 / Motingea & Bonzoi 2008 call Monyɔ́ngɔ a 'C31 ndolo' lect, but Glottolog files Monyongo under Bamwe [bmg] (bamw1238); Donzo 2015 treats Monyongo and Mosange as separate languages (72% lexical similarity).

sources.note: Mosángé (= Ndolo [ndl] per Glottolog) is one of the ten languages described from the author's own fieldwork (p.21: groupement Mosange, Saw river, secteur Ndolo-Liboko, Budjala). Ch.1 §1.3 'La tonologie' pp.62-67: all ten languages have two basic level tones H and L plus derived rising and falling contours; the vowel is the tone-bearing mora; Mosange nominal stems illustrated with H (li-só 'œil'), B (wo 'toi'), H-H (li-tálé 'pierre'), H-B, B-B, B-H, B-B-B, B-B-H, B-H-B schemes; p.44 vowel length not distinctive.
